COURT'S OR JUDGE'S ORDERS
WPMS/1669/2023
Hon'ble Manoj Kumar Tiwari, J.
Ms. Mamta Bisht, Deputy Advocate
General and Mr. Suyash Pant, Standing
Counsel for the State of Uttarakhand /
respondent nos. 1 & 4.
2. This writ petition was filed on
9.6.2023. Registry has pointed out as
many as six defects in the petition and
several opportunities were given to the
petitioner to remove those defects.
3. Since petitioner did not come
forward for removing the defects,
therefore, Registry placed the matter
before this Court. Coordinate Bench vide
order dated 3.11.2023 had granted ten
days time to petitioner for curing the
defects, but despite this order, defects
are not cured.
4. There is no one to represent the
petitioner.
5. By means of this writ petition,
petitioner has sought the following
reliefs:-
"A. During the pendency of instant writ
petition, issue an order or direction or writ, in
the nature of Mandamus commanding the
respondent nos 1, 2,3, and 4 to permit the
petitioner to continue his work from the same
place and provide temporary accommodation
for working otherwise the petitioner shall suffer
irreparable loss and injury, which cannot be
compensated by any means.
B. Issue a writ, in the nature of
Mandamus commanding the respondent nos,

2025:UHC:10326
respondent no 1, 2, 3 and 4 to provide proper
shop in the same place, since the petitioner and
his family has been working in the same place
since more tan 20 years or
C Issue a writ, in the nature of Mandamus
commanding the respondent nos. respondent
no 1, 2, 3 and 4 to provide alternate shop to
continue his business and earn his livelihood."
6. From perusal of the writ petition, it
is revealed that petitioner is selling his
merchandise from a temporary shop
constructed over land belonging to
Bharat Heavy Electricals Ltd.
7. Provisions of Street Vendors
(Protection of Livelihood and Regulation
of Street Vending) Act, 2014 can have no
application to a land belonging to Bharat
Heavy Electricals Ltd. Thus, no protection
can be granted to the writ petitioner in
exercise of power under Article 226 of
the Constitution.
8. The writ petition is, accordingly,
disposed of with liberty to the petitioner
to approach a civil Court for the relief
claimed by him.
 (Manoj Kumar Tiwari, J.)
 20.11.2025
